# Covering Array Tools: the table of best known covering arrays

> An open table of the best known sizes of covering arrays CA(N; t, k, v) and the covering array numbers CAN(t, k, v), with checked arrays, proven lower bounds, credit, constructions and published sources. Site: https://coveringarraytools.org/ . Repository: https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools . Anyone can submit an array by pull request. Every submission is checked before it enters, exactly or, for an array too large for the public exact check, on random column windows until its exact check passes, and credited to the submitter on its row.

The table covers strengths 2 to 6 with at most 25 symbols, binary arrays at strengths 7 to 10, and at most 100,000 columns. Each row gives t, v, k, the size N, its tier (VERIFIED with a checked array, or CITED from the literature with no array here), the source and the credit. A few rows have other tiers: SCREENED (checked on random column windows only, not counted as best known until its exact check passes), DISPUTED (beside a CITED row whose construction, built and checked here, did not give a covering array at that size; the CITED row still counts) and FAILED_PENDING_RECHECK (three rows kept as history). Best known sizes follow the Colbourn rule of table/CONVENTIONS.md, section 4: CITED and VERIFIED rows count. Proven lower bounds are kept per (t, v) and k range, each with the theorem that proves it.

## Read the table

- [coveringarraytools.org](https://coveringarraytools.org/): the table, one cell per (t, v), and a size lookup.
- One page per cell: https://coveringarraytools.org/t{t}/v{v}/ , for example [t3/v3](https://coveringarraytools.org/t3/v3/).
- One JSON and one CSV file per cell, every size step with N, floor, status, credit, construction and the sha256 of its array: https://coveringarraytools.org/t{t}/v{v}.json and https://coveringarraytools.org/t{t}/v{v}.csv , for example [t3/v3.json](https://coveringarraytools.org/t3/v3.json).
- One page per array: https://coveringarraytools.org/ca/{N}/{t}/{k}/{v}/ , with the download link and how to check it.
- [For AI](https://coveringarraytools.org/for-ai/): how to read and cite the data.

## Open targets

- [wanted.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/main/table/wanted.csv): every (t, v, k) that is still open, regenerated on every merge. Columns: best_N (best known size), smallest_array_N (smallest checked array in the table, empty if none), proven_floor, status. status is no_array (no checked array at any size), array_above_best (the best size has no array here, so an array at best_N or smaller is wanted) or beat_best (an array exists at the best size, and a smaller one would be a new record).
- [Wanted: arrays at seven published sizes](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/issues/85)
- [Wanted: arrays for the sizes the table can only cite](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/issues/86)

## How to submit

- [submissions/README.md](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/blob/main/submissions/README.md): the file format, claims.csv, HOW.md and the rules. Open a pull request that adds a folder under submissions/. The check runs on the pull request.
- An array that ties the best size enters as VERIFIED with the submitter's name. A smaller one becomes the new best known size. A larger checked array is recorded as verified but is not a record.
- Arrays withdrawn from the table cannot be submitted or used as a start or an ingredient. The check compares every submission against them.
- The table takes arrays and certificates, not code.

## Data

- [table/ca_table.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/main/table/ca_table.csv): every row of the table.
- [table/lower_bounds.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/main/table/lower_bounds.csv): proven lower bounds with theorem and reference.
- [table/MANIFEST.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/main/table/MANIFEST.csv): every array stored in the repository, with its file name in table/arrays/ (files over 1 MiB are gzip-compressed, .txt.gz), t, v, k, N and the sha256 of its canonical form. Find arrays here, not from a folder listing.
- [table/EXTERNAL.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/main/table/EXTERNAL.csv): arrays kept in a public deposit (Zenodo), with location and sha256.

## Checking an array

- [ca_verify.c](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/blob/main/ca_verify.c) and [ca_verify.py](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools/blob/main/ca_verify.py): exact checkers. Every set of t columns must contain every t-tuple of symbols.

## Licence and citation

The table data is under CC BY 4.0 and the code under the MIT licence, except r/cafast and r/countkernel, which are under GPL (>= 3). Cite the table as C. Smolen, ca-tools: a maintained table of covering arrays, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24168008, and cite the authors of the rows you use.
